prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow is 18.4% of the market value, a solid cash return. Also in its favour: return on capital employed is 21.3%, a strong return on the money in the business; profit grew 18.0% a year on average over three years; and value scores 89 of 100 against the comparison pool. Other areas on this side: what the price asks for the earnings, the quality of the business, growth.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on the recent price trend: momentum scores only 2 of 100 against the comparison pool. Also against it: the share price is 51.0% lower than a year ago; over the past year the share did 48.7 percentage points worse than the Nifty 50; and the share price is 67% below its 52-week high. Other areas on this side: growth, the balance sheet, price behaviour.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 8 points in favour and 8 against give an even split. The pool score is 61 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Hold with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
